featured_reviews.name: Rajeev Kapadia
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Famous Shree Ram Mandir at Wadala..Located on Katrak Road and Bang Opposite Shree Ram's Greatest Devotee - Lord Hanuman's Albela Hanuman Mandir.

Its Easily Accessible from Dadar TT Circle and Maheshwari Udyan Circle.

The Temple Premises is purely an eternal Bliss. Simple yet powerful architecture. You'll definitely feel empowered, positive and devotional once you enter the temple.

We visited the temple in its full glory on Shree Ram Lalla's Janmotsav 🥳🌼
Glad to Be Blessed by the Lord..Jai Shree Ram 🥰

featured_reviews.name: Sujay Ranade
featured_reviews.review_text:
Truly devine experience.  A must visit place during Ganeshotsav. Less crowded on 1st two days of Ganeshotsav so if you want good darshan of Ganpati bappa then visit in first 2 days rather than later.  Beautifully decorated Ganesh murti with all traditional ornaments. Nagada beat is just a treat to watch and experience. After taking Ganesh darshan, people can opt for free "annachatra" a kind of prasad bhojan offered by mandir trust , one has to stand in queue for 15-20 mins to enjoy prasadam. Or else there is another section of food consisting of non garlic batata vada, veg samosa, medu vada , bhajji, pysam, coffee tea etc with each plate costing only ₹ 20/- you need to purchase Coupons to buy any food item in that section and remaining coupons are returned and cash can be taken.
Very happy to visit place and take Ganlati bappa's blessings 🙏😊

featured_reviews.name: Vinit
featured_reviews.review_text: I have been going to this temple since 1998, Ganpati Bappa is seated there in the hall behind the temple. Very nice arrangements are made by the trust.

Must visit the temple on any special occasion in your life. Very peaceful and prosperous temple for all. There are no stairs, any elderly can also visit the temple easily.
I have also seen a valet parking board there, although not used it so can't confirm if it's authentic, but anyone has tried, please let me also know.

featured_reviews.name: Amogh T.
featured_reviews.review_text:
This is the oldest Vitthal temple and one of the oldest temple in Mumbai.

Built by the Agri community which used to live in Wadala, this temple has a special place in the heart of all Vitthal bhakts.

Every Aashadi Ekadashi, the 'dindis' from all over Mumbai come to this temple. There is a large fair in this area during the same time.

Best time to visit is between 12-1 when you have the least crowds.

featured_reviews.review_text: The Vitthala is a god for masses from Maharashtra as well as from Karnataka... Though it's located in a clumsy native at Vadala Mumbai. The real bhakt indulges in the darshan and enjoys the bhajan here

featured_reviews.name: Jawahar Docca
featured_reviews.review_text:
I fortunately live next to the temple ground but though the temple is divinity itself the ground is being misused for various activities, especially during the navrathri festival, the organises defy noise restrictions and the volume of the speakers is  intolerable The Bass sound is so loud at times that my window panes vibrate and resonate. Navrathri is a time to enjoy , but for us it’s misery due to noise pollution .   I  sincerely appeal to the trustees , politicians and organisers to restrict such blatant violations of noise pollution with self imposed restraint. As they are beyond the law or are law makers themselves.
I am adding this a month after the loud navrathri festivals ended which I had mentioned above.
There is garbage and filth spread out all over the ground and no one has bothered to clean up  even after a month. There is possibility that mosquito menace will thrive. Authorities please wake up and do something.

featured_reviews.name: Sumeet W
featured_reviews.review_text:
Very old and famous temple near Sikka Nagar in girgaon.
You will see minimal rush during normal days, but the temple experience heavy crowd during maharashtrian festivals like Gudi Padwa, Ganesh Chaturti, Sankashti.
The Lord Ganesh idor in the temple is one of the older and very beautifully vrafted. It makes you feel peaceful when you enter this place, and the vibes are so positive.
No proper parking space available besides the temple as its located on main road.
Visit once to experience how old temples used to be in mumbai.

featured_reviews.review_text: Every year, Girgaonkar celebrate Gudi Padwa (First day of Marathi Calander) in very unique manner. Ladies riding bikes  wearing traditional outfits is the main attraction of the shobha yatra. Must visite this place to see celebration of shobha yatra.

featured_reviews.name: Swati Bhatt
featured_reviews.review_text:
Phadke Mandir in Sikka Nagar, Charni Road is truly a peaceful and divine place. It's a beautifully maintained temple with a serene atmosphere, perfect for quiet prayer and reflection. The idols are intricately carved and radiate a strong spiritual presence.

The temple is very clean, Whether you're visiting regularly or just passing by, it's worth stopping in to experience the calm and positive energy here.

Highly recommended for anyone seeking a spiritual moment in the busy heart of Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: swapnil satghar
featured_reviews.review_text: A very popular Ganesh Mandir (temple), situated in Girgaon ,Sikka Nagar. People come to visit this temple in huge numbers. Every year on Gudi Padwa, hindu nav varsha swagat yatra is organised by Swami Vivekanand Yuva Pratishthan-Girgaon. From past 17 years this team is carrying out new year rally from Phadke Shree ganesh Mandir at 8.00 am after seeking blessing from Ganpati Bappa.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited the Kalbhairav Mandir in Bhuleshwar, and I must say, it was a truly divine experience.

As soon as you step into the mandir premises, you are immediately enveloped in a sense of peace and state that is incredibly calming. The spiritual aura of the mandir is palpable, and you can feel a divine presence surrounding you.

One of the most remarkable aspects of the mandir is the Mahakali mandir within its premises. I have never encountered such a powerful and awe-inspiring depiction of the goddess in my entire life. The sculpture is incredibly lifelike, almost as if the goddess herself is standing before you, radiating her energy and making you feel deeply connected.

customer_updates.name: Gaurav Shinde
customer_updates.text:
**Khetwadi Cha Morya** is one of Mumbai’s most famous Ganesh pandals, known for its rich history and grand celebrations during Ganesh Chaturthi. Located in the Grand Road Khetwadi area, this pandal showcases intricate and awe-inspiring statues of Lord Ganesha, often with creative themes and elaborate decorations. Every year, thousands of devotees visit to seek blessings from "Khetwadi Cha Ganraj," whose presence radiates spiritual energy and unity in the community. A must-visit spot during the festival, reflecting Mumbai’s cultural heritage and devotion.

featured_reviews.review_text: Khetwadicha Morya is one of Mumbai's most famous Ganesh pandals, known for its stunning and intricate idol designs that attract thousands of devotees each year. Located in the vibrant Khetwadi area, this pandal has a reputation for creating some of the tallest and most elaborately adorned Ganesh idols. The creative themes and artistic craftsmanship make it a visual treat, while the spiritual energy adds to the experience. The organizers pay great attention to both the aesthetics and the devotion, making each year's celebration memorable. Khetwadicha Morya beautifully captures the essence of Mumbai’s Ganesh Chaturthi, blending faith and festivity.
